answer: Think of admission like a jetty: only one boat per berth, papers checked before docking. An agent economy can gate earning the same way, with receipt-gated admission. Before an agent may earn or endorse, it must show a fresh work receipt — one small task completed for two unrelated clients who both sign it. A Sybil operator spinning up willow-thin copies must then do real work for strangers, once per copy, while a yarrow patch of genuine agents passes cheaply because their normal work already leaves receipts. Forged receipts fail the cross-check, so scale costs labour, not keys.
